claim: The previously selected o_proj plus gate/up group-8 INT4 QDQ candidate passed all configured teacher-forced quality-proxy gates against the BF16 baseline over 4,096 contiguous WikiText-2 test targets.

comparison.baseline: Local Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint loaded as BF16.
comparison.candidate: The same checkpoint loaded as BF16, with o_proj and gate/up weights symmetrically quantized to signed INT4 codes in float32 arithmetic, dequantized, and copied back into BF16 parameters.
comparison.metric_accumulation: Per-window logits were converted to float32 for NLL and logit-difference aggregation.
comparison.memory_bound: Both BF16 models remained resident while one baseline/candidate window pair was evaluated at a time; baseline logits were not accumulated across windows.

candidate.selection_provenance: Selected on the earlier hand-authored 15-mask search. Neither this sequential corpus nor its results were used to select the mask.

corpus.target_span: Contiguous token positions 32 through 4,127 of the pinned stream, partitioned into non-overlapping 64-token targets with rolling 32-token contexts.
corpus.benchmark_note: The source and split are standard WikiText-2 data, but this first-4,096-target sequential subset and the configured multi-metric gates are not the canonical full-test benchmark protocol.

estimated_storage.note: Packed storage remains an arithmetic deployment estimate. The measured candidate retained dequantized BF16 weights and did not materialize packed codes, persistent scales, or a packed kernel.

host_observation.process_visibility: Sandbox policy denied ps and top, so individual competing processes could not be inspected.

limitations: Teacher-forced NLL, perplexity, logits, and token agreement are language-modeling proxies, not task accuracy or end-to-end agent success.
Only the first 4,096 target tokens of the 299,078-token pinned stream were evaluated; this is not full WikiText-2 test perplexity.
The candidate was selected on another corpus, but the thresholds were not statistically calibrated and confidence intervals were not estimated.
No packed INT4 kernel, runtime compression, throughput, latency, energy, serving cost, or dollars-per-token improvement was measured.
The result applies to the local Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint and does not establish transfer to a larger model.
conclusion: The selective o_proj plus gate/up mask passed all five predeclared quality-proxy gates in a memory-bounded BF16 comparison over 4,096 contiguous held-out targets. NLL increased by 0.06184 and perplexity by 6.379%, while RMSE, cosine, and top-1 agreement also remained within bounds. This materially strengthens the evidence that selective model-family quantization can preserve next-token behavior better than quantizing every linear layer, but the 24.629% packed-weight reduction is still an unmeasured deployment estimate rather than demonstrated runtime or dollars-per-token savings.
